question: Where was the first session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The inaugural session of the Indian National Congress met on 28 December 1885 in Bombay, at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College (Pathshala) (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस का पहला अधिवेशन — बंबई, दिसंबर 1885)

 

• The meeting was first planned for Poona, but an outbreak of plague in that city made the organisers shift it to Bombay at short notice.

 

• A.O. Hume organised the gathering on the strength of consultations with leading Indians and with the then Viceroy, Lord Dufferin.

 

• Seventy-two delegates attended, and the presidency of the session went to the Calcutta barrister W.C. Bonnerjee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Calcutta hosted the second session (1886) under Dadabhai Naoroji, and Madras the third (1887) under Badruddin Tyabji.

 

• Poona eventually hosted a Congress session in 1895, presided over by Surendranath Banerjee.

 

• Hume had earlier circulated an open letter (1883) to the graduates of Calcutta University, urging them to organise a national body.

 

• The session lasted three days and passed nine resolutions, mostly asking for administrative reforms and wider Indian representation.

 

NOTE

 

• Poona (Option 1): Poona was the originally planned venue, but the outbreak of plague forced a change. It did host a later session in 1895 under Surendranath Banerjee, so it was not the place of the inaugural meeting.

 

• Calcutta (Option 2): Calcutta's turn came a year later: the second session of 1886, with Dadabhai Naoroji presiding, met there. The first meeting had already taken place in Bombay by then.

 

• Madras (Option 3): Madras hosted the third annual session of 1887, famous for Badruddin Tyabji becoming the first Muslim president. It had no role in the founding session of 1885.

question: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is W.C. Bonnerjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee, a leading Calcutta barrister, was the first President of the Congress at the Bombay session of 1885 (कांग्रेस के प्रथम अध्यक्ष — व्योमेश चंद्र बनर्जी)

 

• He presided again at the Allahabad session of 1892, thus becoming one of the few leaders to hold the post twice in the early years.

 

• A.O. Hume, a retired civil servant, was the moving spirit and functioned as the General Secretary, not as the President.

 

• Bonnerjee later settled in England, where he continued to speak for Indian causes and helped the Indian Parliamentary Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bonnerjee's name is often spelt Banerjee in textbooks; he was a Calcutta barrister who later moved to England and remained active in Indian causes.

 

• Allan Octavian Hume served as the first General Secretary of the Congress until 1906.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, 'Grand Old Man of India', presided in 1886, 1893 and 1906.

 

• The Congress held its sessions every December during its early years, in a different city each time to spread its influence.

 

NOTE

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 2): Naoroji was elected to the chair only at the second session in Calcutta in 1886, not the inaugural one. He later presided over the Lahore and Calcutta sessions as well, totalling three terms.

 

• A.O. Hume (Option 3): Hume was the organiser and General Secretary who drove the founding effort, but the presidential chair was given to an Indian, Bonnerjee, to underline the national character of the new body.

 

• Badruddin Tyabji (Option 4): Tyabji became President in 1887 at Madras as the first Muslim to hold the post. He had been among the Bombay leaders who supported the founding meeting but did not preside over it.

question: Which Viceroy was in office when the Indian National Congress was founded in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Dufferin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Dufferin was the Viceroy of India (1884–88) when the Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 (कांग्रेस की स्थापना के समय वायसराय — लॉर्ड डफरिन)

 

• Hume is said to have consulted Dufferin before launching the organisation, and the Viceroy approved of the idea of a body that voiced Indian opinion within constitutional limits.

 

• Dufferin was later reported to have ridiculed the Congress as representing a 'microscopic minority', a remark that revealed official coolness towards it.

 

• The 'safety valve' interpretation of the Congress's birth is linked with this consultation between Hume and Dufferin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Ripon (1880–84) was popular among Indians for the Ilbert Bill and local self-government, and had left India just before the Congress took shape.

 

• Lord Lytton (1876–80) is known for the Vernacular Press Act and the Arms Act.

 

• Lord Lansdowne (1888–94) was Viceroy at the time of the Indian Councils Act, 1892, which the Congress had campaigned for.

 

• Dufferin's tenure also saw the Third Burmese War and the annexation of Upper Burma in 1886.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Ripon (Option 1): Ripon had been Viceroy until 1884 and was a favourite of educated Indians. He departed before the Congress was formed, so he cannot be the Viceroy at its foundation in December 1885.

 

• Lord Lytton (Option 2): Lytton governed from 1876 to 1880, a period of the Vernacular Press Act and the Delhi Durbar. His term had ended five years before the Congress was established.

 

• Lord Lansdowne (Option 4): Lansdowne succeeded Dufferin in December 1888 and oversaw the Councils Act of 1892. He came to office three years after the founding session had already been held.

question:
Match the early political associations with their founders or leaders.

Column A: (a) Bombay Association (b) Madras Native Association (c) East India Association (d) Indian Association

Column B: (i) Dadabhai Naoroji (ii) Surendranath Banerjee (iii) Jagannath Shankarseth (iv) Lakshminarasu Chetty
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bombay Association (1852) was formed by Jagannath Shankarseth, with Dadabhai Naoroji among its prominent members, so a-iii is right (प्रारंभिक राजनीतिक संस्थाएँ और उनके संस्थापक)

 

• The Madras Native Association (1852) was founded by Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty, pairing b with iv.

 

• The East India Association was set up in London in 1866 by Dadabhai Naoroji to place Indian grievances before the British public and Parliament, so c-i holds.

 

• The Indian Association of Calcutta (1876) was the work of Surendranath Banerjee and Anandamohan Bose, giving d-ii.

 

• Together the four correct pairs give a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The British Indian Association (1851) of Bengal, with its organ the Hindu Patriot, was an earlier body of landholders.

 

• The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) was led by Mahadev Govind Ranade, G.V. Joshi and others.

 

• The Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884) and the Bombay Presidency Association (1885) were the last regional bodies before the Congress.

 

• The Indian Association of Calcutta organised the Indian National Conference in 1883, a forerunner of the Congress.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii (Option 2): This swaps the founders of the Bombay and Madras bodies. Shankarseth built the Bombay Association, while Lakshminarasu Chetty belongs to Madras, so the first two pairs cannot be reversed.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 3): The founders of the East India Association and the Indian Association are interchanged here. Naoroji led the London body of 1866, whereas Surendranath Banerjee led the Calcutta body of 1876.

 

• a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii (Option 4): Here the Bombay body is credited to Naoroji and the London association to Shankarseth. Naoroji founded the London East India Association, while Shankarseth led the Bombay Association.

question: The 'Safety Valve Theory' regarding the origin of the Indian National Congress is mainly linked with the role of which person?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A.O. Hume.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Safety Valve Theory, A.O. Hume formed the Congress so that the growing discontent of educated Indians would find a peaceful outlet (सेफ्टी वाल्व सिद्धांत — ए.ओ. ह्यूम)

 

• Some British writers argued that Hume wished to prevent a violent upheaval like the Revolt of 1857, and that official circles encouraged this plan.

 

• The Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 on Hume's suggestion, with the Viceroy Dufferin informally supportive.

 

• Nationalist writers rejected the theory, holding that the Congress emerged from an economic and political awakening and not from an imperial design.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai's writing in Young India is cited among the criticisms of this view.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hume formed the Indian National Union in 1884, which merged into the Congress.

 

• Hume was General Secretary of the Congress from 1885 to 1906 and is remembered as its 'Father'.

 

• Another view, advanced by Bipan Chandra and others, treats the Congress as the product of Indian leaders' own political maturity.

 

• Hume had retired from the Indian Civil Service in 1882.

 

NOTE

 

• W.C. Bonnerjee (Option 1): Bonnerjee presided over the founding session but is not the one credited with the safety valve idea. Historians assign that supposed motive to the organiser, Hume, not to the first President.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 2): Surendranath Banerjee ran the Indian Association and the 1883 National Conference. He was a nationalist agitator whose own separate efforts do not form part of the safety valve argument.

 

• Lord Ripon (Option 4): Ripon, Viceroy until 1884, was liked by Indians for liberal measures. The theory is not about a Viceroy's own scheme but about Hume's alleged purpose in founding the body.

question:
Consider the following statements about the background of the Indian National Congress.

1. A.O. Hume formed the Indian National Union in 1884.

2. The Indian National Conference of 1883 was held in Calcutta.

3. The Indian National Conference of 1883 was organised by A.O. Hume.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Hume founded the Indian National Union in 1884, the body that prepared the ground for the Congress (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय संघ — 1884)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the Indian National Conference met in Calcutta in December 1883 and invited public figures and associations to discuss national issues.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: the 1883 Conference was organised by Surendranath Banerjee and Anandamohan Bose of the Indian Association, not by Hume.

 

• The Conference's second session took place in Calcutta in December 1885, at the very time the Congress was meeting in Bombay, and the two soon merged in purpose.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surendranath Banerjee's arrest in 1883 for contempt of court had stirred nationwide protest and helped create the climate for a national platform.

 

• Hume's open letter of March 1883 to Calcutta University graduates called for 50 volunteers to form a national union.

 

• Because the Conference and Congress overlapped in membership, the Conference was gradually absorbed into the Congress.

 

• The Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883 had also exposed racial attitudes and pushed educated Indians toward organised politics.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): This pairing accepts the Calcutta venue but also credits Hume with the 1883 Conference. The Conference was the creation of the Indian Association leaders, so statement 3 spoils it.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Here the Hume attribution is accepted for both bodies but the Union of 1884 is dropped. The Union is Hume's, yet the Conference was not, so this combination fails.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): This accepts every statement, but the third is incorrect since Hume was not the organiser of the Calcutta Conference of 1883. A set containing it cannot be right.

question: Who, as President of the Congress, used the word 'Swaraj' for the first time from the Congress platform?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, presiding over the Calcutta session of 1906, declared that the goal of Indians was 'self-government or Swaraj like that of the United Kingdom or the colonies' (कांग्रेस मंच से 'स्वराज' शब्द का पहला प्रयोग — दादाभाई नौरोजी, 1906)

 

• This was his third term as President, after 1886 (Calcutta) and 1893 (Lahore).

 

• The same session adopted resolutions on Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education along with Swaraj, reflecting the mood created by the Bengal Partition.

 

• Naoroji was a Moderate yet was chosen in 1906 because he alone could hold the Moderates and Extremists together.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Naoroji authored 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' and put forward the Drain of Wealth theory.

 

• He was elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 as a Liberal member for Finsbury Central.

 

• The Moderate-Extremist rift followed within a year, at Surat in 1907.

 

• He is called the 'Grand Old Man of India'.

 

NOTE

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 1): Tilak popularised the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright' but he never held the Congress presidency, so he did not use the word as President from the platform in 1906.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 2): Gokhale presided at Benares in 1905, a year earlier, and championed constitutional methods. The word Swaraj was not announced as a goal at his session.

 

• Rash Behari Ghosh (Option 4): Rash Behari Ghosh presided over the stormy Surat session of 1907, a year after the Swaraj declaration, and he stood firmly with the Moderate group.

question: Who was the first Muslim to be elected President of the Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badruddin Tyabji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Badruddin Tyabji, a Bombay barrister, presided over the Madras session of 1887, the third session of the Congress (कांग्रेस के प्रथम मुस्लिम अध्यक्ष — बदरुद्दीन तैयबजी)

 

• In his presidential address he appealed to Muslims to join the Congress, arguing that its aims concerned all communities.

 

• Sir Syed Ahmad Khan opposed the Congress, and Tyabji's election was partly an attempt to counter the impression that it was a Hindu body.

 

• Tyabji was also one of the founders of the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rahmatullah M. Sayani presided at Calcutta in 1896, where 'Vande Mataram' was sung at a Congress session for the first time.

 

• Mohammad Ali Jauhar presided over the Kakinada session of 1923.

 

• Hakim Ajmal Khan acted as the President of the Ahmedabad session of 1921, when C.R. Das was in jail.

 

• Abul Kalam Azad later served as President for the Delhi special session 1923 and the Ramgarh session 1940.

 

NOTE

 

• Rahmatullah M. Sayani (Option 2): Sayani was President in 1896 at Calcutta, nine years after Tyabji. He is remembered for the first singing of Vande Mataram at a Congress session, not as the first Muslim president.

 

• Hakim Ajmal Khan (Option 3): Ajmal Khan acted as President in 1921 at Ahmedabad because the elected President was imprisoned. That was decades after Tyabji had set the precedent in 1887.

 

• Mohammad Ali Jauhar (Option 4): Mohammad Ali Jauhar served as President in 1923 at Kakinada, during the Khilafat era. He came far later than the Madras session where the first Muslim president was chosen.

question: Who was the first British (non-Indian) President of the Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is George Yule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• George Yule, a Scottish-born businessman of Calcutta, presided over the Allahabad session of 1888, the fourth session (कांग्रेस के प्रथम ब्रिटिश अध्यक्ष — जॉर्ज यूल, इलाहाबाद 1888)

 

• His election showed that the early Congress welcomed sympathetic Europeans and was keen to win British opinion.

 

• Allahabad became a regular venue, hosting sessions in 1888, 1892 and 1910.

 

• Several Britons later presided: Wedderburn (1889, 1910), Webb (1894) and Cotton (1904).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• William Wedderburn presided at Bombay in 1889 and again at Allahabad in 1910; he was a retired ICS officer and Hume's biographer.

 

• Alfred Webb, an Irish Member of Parliament, presided at Madras in 1894.

 

• Henry Cotton, a former Chief Commissioner of Assam, presided at Bombay in 1904.

 

• Annie Besant, born in London, became the first woman President in 1917.

 

NOTE

 

• William Wedderburn (Option 1): Wedderburn followed in 1889 at Bombay, the fifth session. He was the second British president, so he cannot hold the distinction of the first.

 

• Henry Cotton (Option 3): Henry Cotton presided in 1904 at Bombay, more than fifteen years after Yule. He was a former Assam administrator and did not come first among the British presidents.

 

• Alfred Webb (Option 4): Alfred Webb was an Irish parliamentarian who presided in 1894 at Madras. His election occurred six years after the Allahabad session where the first British president was chosen.

question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was 'Vande Mataram' sung for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta, 1896.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Vande Mataram' was sung for the first time at a Congress session at Calcutta in 1896, when Rahmatullah M. Sayani presided; Rabindranath Tagore sang it (कांग्रेस अधिवेशन में पहली बार वंदे मातरम् — कलकत्ता 1896)

 

• The song, composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, first appeared in the novel Anandamath (1882).

 

• Sayani was a Muslim lawyer from Bombay, so the session showed the Congress's inclusive character even as the song later became a subject of communal debate.

 

• The song became the rallying cry of the Swadeshi movement after the Partition of Bengal in 1905.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anandamath, set against the Sannyasi Rebellion, was serialised in the journal Bangadarshan.

 

• The first two stanzas of Vande Mataram were adopted as the national song by the Constituent Assembly, with equal honour to Jana Gana Mana.

 

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad made the formal statement of this status on 24 January 1950.

 

• Aurobindo Ghosh translated the song into English.

 

NOTE

 

• Benares, 1905 (Option 1): The Benares session of 1905, presided over by Gokhale, took up the Bengal Partition issue and swadeshi support. The song had already been sung at a Congress session nine years earlier.

 

• Calcutta, 1911 (Option 2): The Calcutta session of 1911 is the one at which Jana Gana Mana, and not Vande Mataram, was sung for the first time under Bishan Narayan Dar's presidency.

 

• Madras, 1887 (Option 4): At Madras in 1887 Badruddin Tyabji made his appeal to Muslims. Vande Mataram had not yet reached the Congress platform that early; it came in 1896.

question: The song 'Jana Gana Mana' was sung for the first time at a Congress session held at Calcutta in 1911 under the presidentship of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bishan Narayan Dar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bishan Narayan Dar (Dhar) presided over the Calcutta session of 1911, where Tagore's 'Jana Gana Mana' was sung for the first time on 27 December (कांग्रेस अधिवेशन 1911 — जन गण मन पहली बार, अध्यक्ष बिशन नारायण दर)

 

• The composition was by Rabindranath Tagore, first published as 'Bharat Bhagya Bidhata' in 1912 in a Brahmo journal.

 

• The song was adopted as India's national anthem by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950.

 

• The session was also held just after the Delhi Durbar of 1911, at which the annulment of Bengal's Partition was announced.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dar was a Kashmiri Pandit lawyer from Lucknow and belonged to the Moderate school.

 

• The Delhi Durbar of December 1911 announced the annulment of the Bengal Partition and the shift of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi.

 

• The Constituent Assembly adopted the Anthem and National Song together on 24 January 1950.

 

• Only the first stanza of the five of Tagore's original song is officially the anthem, played in about 52 seconds.

 

NOTE

 

• Madan Mohan Malaviya (Option 2): Malaviya presided at Lahore in 1909 and Delhi in 1918, but not at the Calcutta session of 1911. In 1909 he was a rising Moderate leader and Hindu University advocate.

 

• Rash Behari Ghosh (Option 3): Ghosh presided over the Surat session of 1907 and again at Madras in 1908. The 1911 Calcutta session, where the anthem was first sung, was under a different President.

 

• Ambika Charan Mazumdar (Option 4): Mazumdar presided over the Lucknow session of 1916, which saw the reunion of Moderates and Extremists. That was five years after the Calcutta session of 1911.

question: The Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at the Surat session of 1907. Who was the President of that session?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rash Behari Ghosh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rash Behari Ghosh, a Moderate lawyer-statesman, presided at Surat in December 1907, when the Congress broke into Moderate and Extremist camps (सूरत अधिवेशन 1907 — अध्यक्ष रास बिहारी घोष, कांग्रेस का विभाजन)

 

• The session was originally planned at Nagpur but moved to Surat because the Moderates did not want Tilak's supporters to dominate it.

 

• The Extremists wanted Lala Lajpat Rai as the President, while the Moderates pushed Ghosh; this dispute and the question of Swadeshi and Boycott led to disorder.

 

• The session was suspended without passing any resolution, and the Moderates then held a convention that framed a constitution for the Congress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ghosh presided again at Madras in 1908, when the Moderates controlled an organisation purged of Extremists.

 

• Tilak and Aurobindo led the Extremist group; Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta led the Moderates.

 

• The Congress remained divided until the Lucknow session of 1916, when the two wings reunited.

 

• The Government of Lord Minto took advantage of the split and the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 favoured the Moderates.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 1): Lajpat Rai was the candidate the Extremists wanted for the Surat chair, but the Moderates ensured Ghosh's election. He later presided over the special Calcutta session of 1920.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 2): Naoroji was President in 1906, the year before. He had kept the two groups together at Calcutta with his Swaraj message, but he did not preside at Surat.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 4): Gokhale was President in 1905 at Benares and led the Moderate camp at Surat, yet he was not in the chair. Ghosh was chosen to preside over that session.

question: Who presided over the 1905 Benares session of the Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the Congress session at Benares in 1905, held while the Partition of Bengal was announced and carried out (बनारस अधिवेशन 1905 — अध्यक्ष गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले)

 

• In his address Gokhale condemned the Bengal Partition and Lord Curzon's policies, and the session supported the Swadeshi and Boycott agitation in Bengal.

 

• Gokhale was a leading Moderate and founded the Servants of India Society the same year, 1905.

 

• He was considered Gandhi's political guru; Gandhi acknowledged him as such in his later writings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pherozeshah Mehta presided at Calcutta in 1890, and was known as the 'Uncrowned King of Bombay'.

 

• R.C. Dutt, author of 'Economic History of India', presided at Lucknow in 1899.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee presided at Poona (1895) and Ahmedabad (1902).

 

• Gokhale also presided over the Congress only once, in 1905.

 

• In 1905 Gokhale and Lala Lajpat Rai went to England as a Congress deputation to educate British opinion about Indian demands, just before the session.

 

NOTE

 

• Pherozeshah Mehta (Option 1): Mehta presided at Calcutta in 1890. Though he was a powerful Moderate in Bombay civic politics, the Benares chair of 1905 did not fall to him.

 

• Romesh Chunder Dutt (Option 2): Dutt presided in 1899 at Lucknow and was a respected economic historian. He was not the President when Benares hosted the Congress six years later.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 3): Banerjee presided in 1895 at Poona and in 1902 at Ahmedabad. He was a vocal opponent of the Bengal Partition but did not hold the chair at Benares.

question:
Arrange the following Congress events in chronological order.

1. Badruddin Tyabji becomes the first Muslim President

2. Vande Mataram is sung for the first time at a session

3. The word 'Swaraj' is used from the Congress platform by the President

4. The Congress splits at Surat
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2, 3, 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Badruddin Tyabji presided over the Madras session of 1887, so event 1 comes first (घटनाओं का कालक्रम — 1887, 1896, 1906, 1907)

 

• Vande Mataram was sung at the Calcutta session of 1896 under Rahmatullah Sayani, placing event 2 second.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji used the word Swaraj at Calcutta in 1906, making event 3 the third.

 

• The Surat split occurred in December 1907, which is the last of the four events.

 

• The right order is therefore 1, 2, 3, 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Congress sessions between 1887 and 1907 included Pune (1895), Amraoti (1897), Lucknow (1899) and Benares (1905).

 

• Each of the four events took place during the Moderate phase, ending with the Moderate-Extremist rupture.

 

• Naoroji's 1906 address held that India should enjoy self-government like the colonies.

 

• The Congress reunited in 1916 at Lucknow after a gap of nine years.

 

NOTE

 

• 2, 1, 3, 4 (Option 1): This sequence places the 1896 Vande Mataram event before the 1887 session of Tyabji. Tyabji's presidency at Madras came nine years earlier, so the initial order is faulty.

 

• 1, 3, 2, 4 (Option 3): Here the Swaraj declaration of 1906 is shown before the first Vande Mataram of 1896. The song was sung ten years earlier, so the relative order of these two events is wrong.

 

• 1, 2, 4, 3 (Option 4): This one puts the Surat split before the Swaraj usage. Naoroji's 1906 Calcutta session preceded the 1907 split, so the final two events are interchanged.

question: The Lucknow session of 1916, which saw the reunion of Moderates and Extremists, was presided over by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ambika Charan Mazumdar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ambika Charan Mazumdar presided over the Lucknow session of December 1916, at which the Moderates and Extremists were reunited (लखनऊ अधिवेशन 1916 — अध्यक्ष अंबिका चरण मजूमदार)

 

• The reunion became possible after Tilak's release in 1914 and the Moderates' acceptance of the Extremists, with Annie Besant's Home Rule efforts easing the way.

 

• At the same session the Congress and the Muslim League signed the Lucknow Pact, accepting separate electorates for Muslims and weightage for minorities.

 

• Mohammad Ali Jinnah played a key role in bringing about the Pact and was called an 'ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity' at the time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak's Home Rule League was started in April 1916, and Besant's in September 1916.

 

• The Lucknow Pact reserved one-third of the seats for Muslims in the Imperial Legislative Council.

 

• Mazumdar was a Bengal lawyer from Faridpur, in what is now Bangladesh.

 

• The Pact was a basis for the Montagu-Chelmsford discussions, though the Congress later criticised communal electorates.

 

NOTE

 

• Annie Besant (Option 1): Besant presided in 1917 at Calcutta as the first woman President, after her internment became an issue. The 1916 reunion session had a different chairperson.

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 2): Motilal Nehru presided in 1919 at Amritsar and in 1928 at Calcutta. In 1916 he was still outside the central leadership of the Congress.

 

• Bishan Narayan Dar (Option 3): Dar presided in 1911 at Calcutta, the session where Jana Gana Mana was sung for the first time. The Lucknow session came five years later under another person.

question:
Consider the following statements.

1. Annie Besant was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (Calcutta, 1917).

2. Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress (Kanpur, 1925).

3. Nellie Sengupta presided over the Kanpur session of 1925.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Annie Besant presided at Calcutta in 1917, becoming the Congress's first woman President (प्रथम महिला अध्यक्ष एनी बेसेंट, 1917 कलकत्ता)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Sarojini Naidu chaired the Kanpur session of 1925, the first Indian woman to do so; she was called the 'Nightingale of India'.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: the Kanpur session was Sarojini Naidu's. Nellie Sengupta, a British-born woman, presided over the Calcutta session of 1933.

 

• Besant had been interned by the Government in June 1917, and her election was a protest against that act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besant founded the Home Rule League at Adyar in 1916 and Central Hindu College at Benares.

 

• Naidu's poetry collections include 'The Golden Threshold'; she later became Governor of the United Provinces.

 

• Nellie Sengupta was the wife of J.M. Sengupta and a freedom fighter from England.

 

• The 1933 Calcutta session was held under the shadow of a ban on the Congress.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): This credits Sengupta with the 1925 session, which is incorrect, while leaving out the correct claim about Naidu. Sengupta's term came later, in 1933 at Calcutta.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): This pair includes the false Sengupta statement and drops Naidu's, which is accurate. Sengupta belongs to 1933, not 1925, so the grouping cannot be right.

 

• 3 only (Option 4): Only the third statement is selected here, but it is the false one. The Kanpur chair belonged to Sarojini Naidu, and statements 1 and 2 are both accurate.

question: Who presided over the Amritsar session of the Congress in 1919, which condemned the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Motilal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Motilal Nehru presided at Amritsar in December 1919, held a few months after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of April 1919 (अमृतसर अधिवेशन 1919 — अध्यक्ष मोतीलाल नेहरू)

 

• The session condemned the massacre, criticised the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms as inadequate and disappointing, and took up the Khilafat question.

 

• Amritsar was chosen to honour the victims of the massacre, which had taken place in the same city.

 

• Motilal later presided again at Calcutta in 1928, and he co-founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 with C.R. Das.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Hunter Committee was appointed by the Government to inquire into the Punjab disorders, while the Congress set up its own inquiry under Gandhi, Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das.

 

• The Government of India Act, 1919, was passed in December 1919, the same month as the session.

 

• Motilal Nehru headed the Nehru Report of 1928.

 

• His son Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lahore session of 1929.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 1): Lajpat Rai presided over the special Calcutta session of 1920 that backed the Non-Cooperation Movement. He was not in the chair at the Amritsar session of the year before.

 

• Madan Mohan Malaviya (Option 2): Malaviya presided at Lahore in 1909 and Delhi in 1918, but the Amritsar chair of 1919 was taken by another leader.

 

• C.R. Das (Option 3): C.R. Das presided over the Gaya session of 1922. In 1919 he was a leading member of the Congress inquiry committee on Punjab, not the President at Amritsar.

question: The special session of the Congress held at Calcutta in September 1920, which approved the Non-Cooperation Movement, was presided over by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the special Calcutta session of September 1920, which endorsed Gandhi's Non-Cooperation programme (कलकत्ता विशेष अधिवेशन 1920 — अध्यक्ष लाला लाजपत राय)

 

• The resolution to launch non-cooperation was moved by Gandhi and carried, though many leaders had initially been reluctant to accept it.

 

• The programme included surrender of titles, boycott of courts, schools and legislative councils, and promotion of Swadeshi and Khadi.

 

• The decision was confirmed at the regular Nagpur session of December 1920, presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lajpat Rai, called the 'Punjab Kesari', had earlier been deported to Mandalay in 1907.

 

• The Nagpur session changed the Congress constitution to aim at attainment of Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means.

 

• C.R. Das, who at Calcutta had opposed the boycott of councils, accepted the programme at Nagpur.

 

• He died in 1928 following injuries received in a lathi-charge on a protest against the Simon Commission.

 

NOTE

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 1): Motilal Nehru, who presided in 1919, supported non-cooperation but did not chair the special session of 1920. Lajpat Rai occupied the chair on that occasion.

 

• C.R. Das (Option 2): Das opposed the boycott of legislative councils at the special session; he was not in the chair, and presided over the Gaya session only in 1922.

 

• Vijayaraghavachariar (Option 4): Vijayaraghavachariar presided over the regular Nagpur session in December 1920, which followed the Calcutta special session. He did not chair the September special meeting.

question: Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the Congress three times. Which of the following sessions was NOT presided over by him?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surat, 1907.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Naoroji did not preside at Surat in 1907; that session was chaired by the Moderate Rash Behari Ghosh (नौरोजी ने सूरत 1907 की अध्यक्षता नहीं की — तीन बार अध्यक्ष: 1886, 1893, 1906)

 

• His three terms were Calcutta 1886, Lahore 1893 and Calcutta 1906, spread over twenty years.

 

• At Lahore in 1893 he presided in the year after he was elected to the British House of Commons.

 

• At Calcutta in 1906 he gave Swaraj as the Congress goal, which became a defining moment of the Extremist-Moderate balance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Naoroji was nicknamed the 'Grand Old Man of India' and was the first Asian elected to the British Parliament.

 

• He founded the East India Association in London in 1866 and wrote 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

 

• He was a Parsi who, in 1851, helped found the Rahnumae Mazdayasnan Sabha.

 

• Naoroji also lived long enough to see the Surat split, dying in 1917.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta, 1886 (Option 1): Calcutta 1886 was the second session and Naoroji's first term as President, so this session was presided over by him and cannot be the answer.

 

• Lahore, 1893 (Option 3): Lahore 1893 was his second term, held a year after his election to the House of Commons. As he presided there, it is not the exception asked for.

 

• Calcutta, 1906 (Option 4): Calcutta 1906 was his third term and the occasion of the Swaraj declaration. He presided there, so it cannot be the session he missed.

question: Mahatma Gandhi presided over only one session of the Indian National Congress. At which place was it held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Belgaum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session of December 1924, the only occasion on which he occupied the Congress chair (गांधीजी की अध्यक्षता वाला एकमात्र अधिवेशन — बेलगाम 1924)

 

• Belgaum (now in Karnataka) was then in the Bombay Presidency, and the session was held a year after the Khilafat-Non-Cooperation wave had subsided.

 

• The session met against the background of the Swaraj Party's growing strength in the legislatures and the Government's repressive Bengal Ordinance.

 

• Gandhi stressed Hindu-Muslim unity, removal of untouchability and Khadi in his address.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi never held office in the Congress again after 1924 but guided it informally.

 

• The Swaraj Party of C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru had been formed in 1923 to contest the legislative councils.

 

• A Gandhi-Das-Nehru pact in November 1924 allowed the Swarajists to work as a Congress organ within councils.

 

• Gandhi turned 55 during that year.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagpur (Option 2): Nagpur hosted the regular session of December 1920 that adopted the Non-Cooperation programme and a new constitution, under Vijayaraghavachariar. Gandhi did not preside there.

 

• Karachi (Option 3): Karachi hosted the 1931 session under Vallabhbhai Patel, which endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Gandhi attended it as the main figure but was not the President.

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 4): Ahmedabad hosted the session of December 1921, when C.R. Das was the elected President but was jailed, and Hakim Ajmal Khan acted in his place. Gandhi did not preside.

question: Who became the youngest President of the Indian National Congress at the Delhi special session of 1923?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abul Kalam Azad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad became the youngest Congress President when he presided over the special Delhi session of 1923, at about 35 years of age (कांग्रेस के सबसे युवा अध्यक्ष — अबुल कलाम आज़ाद, दिल्ली 1923)

 

• The special session was called to resolve the dispute between the Pro-Changers (Swarajists) and the No-Changers over entry into legislative councils.

 

• It allowed the Swarajists to contest the council elections, while remaining within the Congress.

 

• Azad returned to the presidency in 1940 at Ramgarh and served continuously until 1946.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Azad edited the weekly Al-Hilal and later Al-Balagh, and was independent India's first Education Minister.

 

• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1992.

 

• The Swaraj Party had been founded in 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru was 40 when he first became President in 1929.

 

NOTE

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 1): Jawaharlal Nehru first presided at Lahore in 1929, at the age of about 40. That was older than Azad's age at his 1923 presidency, so he does not hold the youngest-President record.

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose (Option 2): Bose presided at Haripura in 1938 and Tripuri in 1939, when he was around forty-one and forty-two years old, far older than the 1923 President.

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 4): Rajendra Prasad became President in 1934 at Bombay and again in 1939, when he was around fifty. His age was well beyond that of the 1923 President.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress (1929).

1. It was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

2. It declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as the goal of the Congress.

3. It endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Jawaharlal Nehru presided at Lahore in December 1929, becoming President at the age of about 40 (लाहौर अधिवेशन 1929 — अध्यक्ष जवाहरलाल नेहरू, पूर्ण स्वराज)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the session declared Purna Swaraj as the Congress's goal and authorised the Working Committee to launch civil disobedience.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931 and was endorsed at the Karachi session of 1931, not at Lahore.

 

• The session designated 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day, celebrated through pledge-taking across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tricolour was hoisted by Nehru on the banks of the Ravi on the midnight of 31 December 1929.

 

• The Congress also decided to boycott the Round Table Conference at Lahore.

 

• The Civil Disobedience Movement began with the Dandi March on 12 March 1930.

 

• Nehru's election was backed by Gandhi, who overlooked the claims of Patel.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): This option includes the Gandhi-Irwin Pact for Lahore, which is wrong because the pact came in March 1931. It also leaves out the true claim about the presidency of Nehru.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): This pairs the correct Purna Swaraj resolution with the false pact statement. The pact followed Lahore by more than a year and was approved at Karachi, so the combination fails.

 

• 3 only (Option 4): This choice accepts the Nehru presidency but adds the pact, which was a 1931 event. Lahore passed the Purna Swaraj resolution, making statement 2 part of the right answer, and it is left out here.

question: At the Lahore session of 1929, the tricolour flag was hoisted by Jawaharlal Nehru on the bank of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the bank of the Ravi at Lahore at midnight on 31 December 1929, after the Purna Swaraj resolution (लाहौर 1929 — रावी नदी के तट पर तिरंगा)

 

• The Ravi, one of the five rivers of Punjab, flows through Lahore, which was the venue of the session.

 

• The flag-hoisting was followed by the first observance of Independence Day on 26 January 1930, when the Purna Swaraj pledge was read across India.

 

• Gandhi drafted the Independence pledge issued for that day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 26 January was later chosen as the date for the Constitution to come into force in 1950, to honour the 1930 pledge.

 

• Lahore was the capital of the Punjab Province and is now in Pakistan.

 

• The Karachi session of 1931 formally adopted the saffron-white-green flag with the charkha, and the Ashoka Chakra replaced the wheel in 1947.

 

• Pingali Venkayya designed the original Congress flag.

 

NOTE

 

• Sabarmati (Option 2): The Sabarmati flows past Ahmedabad and Gandhi's Ashram, from where the Dandi March began in 1930. It does not flow past Lahore, where the flag was hoisted.

 

• Ganga (Option 3): The Ganga flows through Kanpur, Allahabad and Benares, none of which hosted the 1929 session. Lahore is on the Ravi, not the Ganga.

 

• Yamuna (Option 4): The Yamuna flows through Delhi and Agra and is far from the Punjab plains around Lahore. The 1929 flag-hoisting took place on the Ravi's bank.

question: Which session of the Indian National Congress adopted a resolution on Fundamental Rights and a national economic programme for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karachi, 1931.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Karachi session of March 1931, presided over by Vallabhbhai Patel, passed the resolution on Fundamental Rights and economic policy (कराची अधिवेशन 1931 — मौलिक अधिकार प्रस्ताव, अध्यक्ष सरदार पटेल)

 

• The resolution, drafted mainly by Jawaharlal Nehru, promised civil liberties, equality before law, free primary education and nationalisation of key industries.

 

• The session also endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 and approved Gandhi as the Congress's representative to the Second Round Table Conference.

 

• It was held soon after the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru, which created a tense atmosphere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Karachi resolution is considered a forerunner of the Fundamental Rights in the Constitution of India.

 

• Gandhi was greeted with black flags by youths at Karachi in protest at the execution.

 

• Patel presided over only the Karachi session during his career.

 

• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact is also known as the Delhi Pact.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore, 1929 (Option 1): The Lahore session of 1929 is known for the Purna Swaraj resolution and the decision to launch civil disobedience; it did not pass the Fundamental Rights resolution that came two years later.

 

• Faizpur, 1937 (Option 3): Faizpur 1937 is famous as the first session in a village and for its agrarian programme. The first Fundamental Rights resolution had already been passed at Karachi.

 

• Haripura, 1938 (Option 4): Haripura 1938 under Subhas Bose discussed the planning of the economy and opposed the federal scheme. It came seven years after the Karachi session that had adopted Fundamental Rights.

question:
Assertion (A): The Faizpur session of the Congress (1937) is regarded as a unique session in the Congress's history.

Reason (R): It was the first session of the Congress to be held in a village.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Faizpur session of December 1937 in Maharashtra, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, was the first Congress session held in a village, which is why it is called unique (फैजपुर अधिवेशन 1937 — पहला ग्रामीण अधिवेशन)

 

• Assertion A is true, because the session's distinctive character comes from its rural setting, a departure from the earlier practice of meeting in big towns.

 

• Reason R is true and gives the exact basis of the uniqueness, so it correctly explains A.

 

• The session was meant to draw the peasantry into the national movement and adopted an agrarian programme demanding lower rent and revenue and a living wage for agricultural labourers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Faizpur is in the Jalgaon district of Maharashtra, then part of Bombay Presidency.

 

• Nehru had been President also in 1936 at Lucknow, which was the first of his consecutive terms.

 

• The 1937 session followed the Congress's victory in the provincial elections held under the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

• Gandhi's Wardha-based constructive programme encouraged the village focus.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This statement says R does not explain A, but it does: the Faizpur session was exceptional chiefly because it took place in a village, so the reason is the actual basis of the assertion.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): This claims R is false. The Faizpur meeting really was the first Congress session in a rural setting, so the reason is valid and the assertion's truth is not matched by a false reason.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): This says A is false, but Faizpur is indeed regarded as unique, and R is true as well. Denying the assertion contradicts the established description of the session.
